text: A while loop always runs its body at least once, then checks the condition afterward to decide whether to repeat.
A for loop can only count upward and cannot decrease its counter or use a custom step size.
A do-while loop checks its condition before the first iteration, so the body may never execute.
A switch statement evaluates every case branch in order regardless of matches, executing all of them.
An expression and a statement are the same thing; both always produce a value.
The return keyword prints a value to the console and then continues executing the rest of the method.
When you call a method, the arguments are always passed by reference, so changes inside always affect the caller.

An if statement can only test numeric values, not boolean or string conditions.

In Python you must declare a variable's data type explicitly before assigning a value to it.
Dynamic typing means a variable's type is fixed permanently once it is first assigned.
Dividing two integers in Python with / always returns an integer, never a decimal.
A variable declared inside a function in Python is automatically accessible everywhere in the program.
The input() function in Python returns an integer whenever the user types a number.

Converting a float to an int in Python rounds it to the nearest whole number.

A class cannot be used as a data type for a variable or parameter.

Two objects created from the same class are always considered equal because they have the same type.

In binary, each position represents a power of 10, just like in decimal.
